title: Prepared Or Unprepared? Evaluating Healthcare Workforce Readiness for Clinical Adoption of Artificial Intelligence in Nigeria
abstract: arXiv:2609.19096v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into healthcare systems worldwide, yet its successful clinical adoption depends critically on workforce readiness, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) where infrastructural and training gaps persist. This cross-sectional study evaluated awareness, attitudes, preparedness, and barriers to AI adoption among 761 healthcare professionals across multiple disciplines and practice settings in Nigeria. Data were collected between December 2025 and March 2026 using a structured, validated questionnaire. Overall awareness of AI in healthcare was high (92.6%); however, objective knowledge and self-reported preparedness remained limited, with 40.9% reporting low or very low knowledge and only 63.0% feeling adequately prepared. Willingness to adopt AI was high: 92.5% expressed interest in training, and 78.7% supported inclusion of AI education in undergraduate curricula. K

translated_title: 准备好了还是没准备好？评估尼日利亚医疗人员对人工智能临床应用的准备程度
translated_abstract: 人工智能（AI）正日益融入全球医疗系统，但其成功的临床应用在很大程度上取决于医疗人员的准备程度，尤其是在基础设施和培训差距持续存在的中低收入国家（LMICs）。这项横断面研究评估了尼日利亚761名来自多个学科和执业环境的医疗专业人员对AI应用的认知、态度、准备程度及障碍。数据于2025年12月至2026年3月间通过结构化、经验证的问卷收集。总体而言，医疗人员对AI的认知度很高（92.6%）；然而，客观知识和自我报告的准备程度仍然有限，40.9%的受访者报告其AI知识水平低或非常低，仅有63.0%的受访者认为自己准备充分。采用AI的意愿很高：92.5%的受访者表示有兴趣接受培训，78.7%支持将AI教育纳入本科课程体系。
tldr: 该研究评估了尼日利亚761名医疗专业人员对AI的认知与准备度，发现尽管AI认知度高（92.6%）且采用意愿强烈，但客观知识和准备程度仍明显不足，凸显了在中低收入国家加强医疗人员AI培训与教育的迫切需求。
en_tdlr: This cross-sectional study of 761 Nigerian healthcare professionals reveals that despite high AI awareness (92.6%) and strong willingness to adopt, objective knowledge and self-reported preparedness remain limited, underscoring the urgent need for AI training and education in LMICs.
